transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I'm feeling really overwhelmed and distressed about the terrible acne and scars on my face. It makes me feel so self-conscious all the time, even though other people tell me they can barely notice anything wrong with my skin.
Can you tell me more about what you do to try to hide or improve the appearance of your skin, and how much time do you spend thinking about your acne and scars each day?

I easily spend three or four hours every day obsessing over my skin and trying to fix it. Before I can even leave the house, I have to spend ages applying layers of heavy makeup under very specific lighting, and I often wear hats or sunglasses to hide my face. It's completely exhausting.
Aside from your concerns about your skin, how have you been feeling overall lately, and have you noticed any changes in your interest in activities or hobbies that you normally enjoy?

I haven't really noticed any major changes in my general mood or my interest in hobbies. It's just that my skin is constantly on my mind, and that is the main thing causing me all this stress and keeping me from wanting to go out.

How has your preoccupation with your skin affected your daily life, such as your relationships, work, or social interactions, and are there any situations that you avoid because of your concerns about your appearance?

My preoccupation with my skin has severely affected my daily life, and I'm constantly late for work because I spend hours trying to camouflage my face with makeup. I've also started avoiding social gatherings and seeing my friends altogether because I'm just too embarrassed for anyone to see me.
Is your concern about your skin primarily focused on the acne and scars, or do you also worry about other aspects of your appearance, such as your nose, eyes, or overall facial structure?

To be honest, it's not just my skin. I also worry a lot about my nose and my eyes because they look completely abnormal and asymmetric to me. It feels like my whole face is just off-balance and wrong.

Have you ever considered seeking surgical or other medical procedures to correct the perceived flaws in your appearance, and do you think that fixing these issues would significantly improve your life and reduce your distress?

Yes, I've actually consulted with several dermatologists and plastic surgeons to see if they can fix my nose and skin. I strongly believe that undergoing these procedures is the only way I will ever feel comfortable in my own skin and finally get some relief from this distress.

Do you think that even if you were to undergo these surgical procedures and they turned out perfectly, your concerns about your appearance would completely disappear, or might you still find something else to worry about?

To be honest, I worry that even if the surgeries went perfectly, I might still find another flaw to be anxious about. My concerns tend to shift, and because my skin, nose, and facial symmetry all feel so wrong, it is hard to imagine ever being completely at peace with my appearance. I'm afraid there would always be something else that would start to bother me.
